speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a concerning rash and recent health changes; to begin my assessment, when did these symptoms first appear and what does the rash look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: That new onset cough and arthritis management are concerning; are you currently taking any new medications, specifically for your recent diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and inflammatory markers are normal, which is helpful. Since you recently started medication for rheumatoid arthritis and developed a rash last night, are you aware of any new side effects listed on your medication label? Also, besides the cough, have you experienced any shortness of breath or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned mucositis and a rash on the upper back; have you experienced any oral sores, diarrhea, or skin peeling in other areas besides your back? REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear_Antibody, Direct_Antinuclear_Antibody, Liver_Function_Tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to new rheumatoid arthritis medication.
